rationale: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1050, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_2017 iter-7 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: batch_size 2 -> 1. BASE_ITER=5 (the BEST + only above-baseline point: SSIM 0.8114, hr 0.0319, ep19/bs2/lr5e-4/lambda0.0023/n_filters16) -- reverting AWAY from iter-6 (lr 3e-4 REGRESSED to 0.7883/hr0). epochs traded 19->10 purely to fit the HARD 1200s budget at bs=1 (NOT a second hypothesis knob); max_train_s 1100->1050 backstop. TRAJECTORY (corrected metric): iter-1 OOM(bs4); iter-2 0.8012 hr0; iter-3 0.7932 hr0 (lambda 0.0023->0.05 REGRESSED); iter-4 0.7828 hr0 (n_filters 16->4 REGRESSED); iter-5 0.8114 hr0.0319 KEEP (epochs 14->19, FIRST above the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor, under-training diagnosis CONFIRMED); iter-6 0.7883 hr0 DISCARD (lr 5e-4->3e-4 REGRESSED -- lower lr starved the under-trained net, iter-6 falsifier TRIGGERED). best hr = 0.0319 @iter-5. LIMITER (box2): under-convergence at the wall-pinned epoch budget. iter-5 confirmed the epochs lever works but ep19 is WALL-PINNED (one more epoch overruns 1200s at 56.4s/epoch bs=2); iter-6 proved lr-down does not help (it starves, not stabilizes). The ONLY remaining within-budget step-count lever is batch_size DOWN: bs=1 doubles batches/epoch (train_n=200 -> 200 batches/epoch vs 100 at bs=2), i.e. doubles optimizer steps per epoch -- the iter-6 PRE-REGISTERED falsifier path (iter-6: if hr<=0.0319, iter-7 must trade gradient STEPS via batch_size 2->1). ONE KNOB CHOICE (box3): batch_size 2->1, base = iter-5 BEST (lr=5e-4 RESTORED, lambda=0.0023, n_filters=16, vn_T=5, kernel=11, n_bumps=31, x_range=2.0, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, seed=42 all held). HYPOTHESIS (box4): bs=1 gives 2x optimizer steps/epoch; even with epochs traded 19->10 the step count rises 1900 (bs2 x ep19) -> 2000 (bs1 x ep10 x 200/epoch), and each step on a smaller batch is a noisier/finer descent that the under-trained VN benefits from -> predict val_ssim rises above 0.8114 (hr > 0.0319), targeting ~0.82-0.83 / hr ~0.04-0.06. FALSIFIER (terminal): if hr <= 0.0319 at bs=1, hammernik_2017s 20-min budget is genuinely convergence-bounded -- doubling steps via bs-down cannot reach the proven ep38/bs1 (7600-step) convergence basin within 1200s -> its ceiling is ~0.032 and the budget-bounded ceiling is DOCUMENTED (no within-budget step-count lever remains: epochs wall-pinned, lr-down failed, bs already at the minimum). BUDGET (box5, HARD 1200s train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): bs=1 doubles batches/epoch AND loses within-batch parallelism + adds per-sample projector swaps, so per-epoch wall rises from 56.4s (bs2) to ~95-105s (bs1, ~1.7-1.9x). At ~105s/epoch x 10 epochs = ~1050s train + ~95s score(214)+figure = ~1145s predicted elapsed < 1200s; max_train_s=1050 backstop trips before the figure, well under the 1800s SLURM kill. If per-epoch lands lighter (~95s) the max_train_s wall stops training at ~ep11, still in-budget. MEMORY-SAFE (SAFER than bs=2): batch_size=1 HALVES the (B,F,H,W)=(1,16,512,512) x 31-bump RBF activation tensors held across 5 unrolled steps vs bs=2 -- strictly less than the iter-5 footprint that already fit 16 GB (bs=4 was the OOM, bs=1 is the safest point). N_k=16, grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability).
